title: Eromba with Ngari (Fermented Fish)
steps: Boil or steam seasonal vegetables until soft. Mash with roasted ngari and plenty of chilli.
Garnish with fresh maroi herbs. Serve with rice – the iconic spicy mashed side of Manipur.

fullIngredients.name: Boiled vegetables (potato, bamboo shoot, beans, etc.)
Ngari (fermented fish), red chilli or umorok

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Ngari is the soul of Eromba – this is the classic non-vegetarian version.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Heat level can be adjusted but authentic versions are fiery.

title: Eromba (Vegetarian)
steps: Boil or steam seasonal vegetables until soft. Mash with fried chives/onion, ginger and plenty of chilli.
Garnish with fresh maroi herbs. Serve with rice – a vegetarian version of the iconic dish.

fullIngredients.name: Boiled vegetables (potato, bamboo shoot, beans, etc.)
Fried chives or onion, ginger, red chilli or umorok

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of Eromba using fried chives instead of ngari.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Still packed with flavour and heat.

title: Singju (Vegetarian)
steps: Mix finely shredded vegetables with roasted sesame powder, a little gram flour, chilli, onion and local herbs.
Toss well and serve as a spicy, crunchy salad or snack.

fullIngredients.name: Finely chopped cabbage, green papaya, other seasonal vegetables
Roasted sesame powder, gram flour, chilli, herbs, onion

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and home salad – refreshing yet spicy.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh.

title: Singju with Ngari (Non-Vegetarian)
steps: Mix finely shredded vegetables with roasted sesame powder, a little gram flour, chilli, onion and local herbs.
Add ngari. Toss well and serve as a spicy, crunchy salad or snack.

fullIngredients.name: Finely chopped cabbage, green papaya, other seasonal vegetables
Roasted sesame powder, gram flour, chilli, herbs, onion

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and home salad with the addition of ngari.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh.

title: Chamthong (Kangshoi) with Ngari
steps: Boil seasonal vegetables with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli in water to make a light stew.
Add ngari or smoked fish for flavour. Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice – an everyday light vegetable stew.

fullIngredients.name: Ngari or smoked fish, onion, ginger, garlic, chilli

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Also called Kangshoi or Kangsoi – minimal oil, maximum freshness.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: This is the classic non-vegetarian version with ngari.

title: Ooti
steps: Cook rice with onion, ginger, peas or seasonal vegetables and a pinch of baking soda (or traditional khar) until soft and slightly thickened.
Season simply. Serve as a comforting one-pot vegetarian dish.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, ginger, baking soda or traditional alkaline water, spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Meitei vegetarian preparation – the alkaline note is traditional.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often made for religious or special occasions when non-veg is avoided.

title: Chagem Pomba
steps: Cook broken rice with mustard greens, hawaijar, smoked fish, onion and peas into a thick, flavourful mixture.
Simmer till everything is soft and well combined.
Serve with rice or as a main – a hearty fermented-soybean dish.

fullIngredients.name: Broken rice, mustard leaves or greens
Hawaijar (fermented soybean), smoked fish, peas, onion

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Hawaijar gives a unique fermented depth.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard leaves are the preferred green.

title: Kanghou
steps: Heat a little mustard oil, add chilli and onion and quickly stir-fry the finely chopped vegetables.
Season with salt and herbs. Keep the vegetables crisp-tender.
Serve as a dry side with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, chilli, onion, local herbs, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple stir-fried vegetable side – light and everyday.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal oil is traditional.

title: Nga Thongba (Fish Curry)
steps: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry or cook in a gravy of onion, ginger, garlic and chilli in mustard oil.
Simmer till the fish is done. Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fish is central to Meitei meals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil and local herbs define the flavour.

title: Pork with Bamboo Shoot
steps: Cook pork with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli until tender. Add bamboo shoot and continue cooking till flavours meld.
Serve with rice – popular especially in hill communities and among non-Meitei groups.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bamboo shoot balances the richness of the pork.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fermented bamboo shoot adds extra tang.

title: Kabok (Sweet Puffed Rice)
steps: Melt jaggery with a little water until syrupy. Toss with puffed rice until well coated.
Shape into balls or leave loose. A classic sweet snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple sweet puffed-rice snack enjoyed across Manipur.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Popular during festivals.

title: Kabok (Savoury Puffed Rice)
steps: Toss puffed rice with finely chopped onion, green chilli, salt and light spices.
Serve as a crunchy savoury snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple savoury puffed-rice snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A quick and easy snack option.

title: Bora (Pakora)
steps: Make a batter of gram flour with chopped onion, local herbs, chilli and salt.
Deep-fry spoonfuls till golden and crisp.
Serve hot as a tea-time or evening snack.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, local herbs, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Manipuri-style fritters – often enjoyed with tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh.

title: Morok Metpa
steps: Boil or roast chilli with ngari. Pound or grind into a coarse, fiery paste with garlic and salt.
Serve as a pungent side with rice and other dishes.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Essential chilli-ngari chutney of Manipuri meals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Extremely spicy – use with caution.

title: Chakhao Kheer
steps: Cook the black rice in milk with sugar or jaggery and cardamom until creamy and the rice is soft.
Garnish with nuts and raisins if desired.
Serve warm or chilled – a special dessert or festive dish.

fullIngredients.name: Milk, sugar or jaggery, cardamom, nuts

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Chakhao is the aromatic black rice of Manipur – nutty and fragrant.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A prized preparation for celebrations.
